finding.claim: Broken access control: the /admin/users/<uid>/ban handler wraps require_admin() in try/except Exception. abort(403) raises an HTTPException, which is caught, logged at warning level, and swallowed. Execution continues to do_ban(uid), so any authenticated non-admin user can ban any user. The sibling unban handler calls require_admin without the try/except and is enforced correctly.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, the privileged ban operation

trace.note: Route entry: POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban, uid taken from the URL
abort(403) raises werkzeug HTTPException for non-admins
Only logs a warning; there is no return, abort or re-raise
do_ban(uid) runs regardless of the admin check result

finding.guards_checked: require_admin is correct in itself (admin.py:9-11) but its result is neutralised by the catch-all handler. There is no other auth middleware or before_request hook in the repo, which is a single file. The sibling unban at admin.py:26 calls require_admin unguarded and is SAFE.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 for non-admins, but the call at admin.py:17 sits inside try/except Exception (admin.py:16-19). The HTTPException is swallowed with only a log.warning, and do_ban runs at line 20. No before_request hook or other middleware exists; admin.py is the only file.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:16-20 the 403 from require_admin is caught by `except Exception` and only logged, so do_ban(uid) executes for any authenticated non-admin. The unban handler at admin.py:26 calls require_admin without a try/except and is therefore safe.
